G1 Sim2Sim MuJoCo

Robotics · unitree_mujoco · G1 Sim2Sim

Test a G1 policy in MuJoCo before the real robot

7 steps in the order they were done. Running example: model_30000.pt from training run g1_tracking/2026-11-04_13-10-18, motion dance1_subject2, driven without a physical gamepad.

How the work flows

model_30000.ptPyTorch checkpoint (not used directly)
→
policy.onnxexported automatically with each checkpoint
→
g1_ctrlC++ controller that reads the ONNX and npz
→
unitree_mujocovirtual robot, DDS over lo
→
Real G1only after the sim is stable
1

Put the ONNX policy in the deploy folder

Terminal · unitree_rl_mjlab · 1 min

Replace the sample Mimic policy with the policy from model 30000.

Good to know

  • Deployment only uses policy.onnx; it never reads .pt files.
  • The tracking runner re-exports policy.onnx on every checkpoint save. The file in the log folder has the same timestamp as model_30000.pt, so it is model 30000.
  • The run's params/env.yaml shows the motion is dance1_subject2.npz, matching the existing Mimic_Dance1_subject2 state.
  • The new ONNX file embeds its weights, so no policy.onnx.data is needed.

Commands

cd "/home/daikai/Robot Unitree/unitree_rl_mjlab/deploy/robots/g1/config/policy/mimic/dance1_subject2/exported"
mkdir -p backup_old && mv policy.onnx policy.onnx.data backup_old/
cp "/home/daikai/Robot Unitree/unitree_rl_mjlab/logs/rsl_rl/g1_tracking/2026-11-04_13-10-18/policy.onnx" .
ls -la
Exit checkls -la shows the new policy.onnx and a backup_old folder.
Actual result: policy.onnx is 991,955 bytes; the old files (14,216 + 990,416 bytes) are in backup_old/.

Output

exported/policy.onnx
2

Install the required libraries

Terminal · needs sudo · 5–10 min

Install Boost, yaml-cpp and unitree_sdk2 (with CycloneDDS), needed by both g1_ctrl and the simulator.

What to do

  1. Install the system packages with apt.
  2. Clone unitree_sdk2 into ~ before building it.
  3. Install it into /usr/local.
  4. Run sudo ldconfig so the system finds libddsc.so.0.

The sudo password prompt shows no characters while typing. A wrong password prints "Sorry, try again".

Commands

sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y \
  libboost-program-options-dev libyaml-cpp-dev \
  libeigen3-dev libfmt-dev libspdlog-dev \
  zlib1g-dev libglfw3-dev

cd ~ && git clone https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_sdk2.git
cd ~/unitree_sdk2 && mkdir -p build && cd build
cmake .. -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local
make -j8 && sudo make install

sudo ldconfig
Exit checkls /usr/local/lib lists libddsc.so.0, libddscxx.so.0 and libunitree_sdk2.a.

Output

unitree_sdk2 + CycloneDDSBoost, yaml-cpp
3

Build the g1_ctrl controller

Terminal · deploy/robots/g1 · 1 min

Compile the controller that runs the policy; the same binary is used in simulation and on the real robot.

cd "/home/daikai/Robot Unitree/unitree_rl_mjlab/deploy/robots/g1"
rm -rf build && mkdir build && cd build
cmake .. && make -j8
Exit checkLast line: [100%] Built target g1_ctrl.

If it says "Could NOT find Boost" or unitree_sdk2 is missing: go back to step 2, then delete build and run again.

Output

Configure and build unitree_mujoco

Terminal + editor · 2 min

Set up the 29-DoF G1 in MuJoCo, talking to g1_ctrl over the lo interface.

What to do

  • unitree_mujoco/simulate is missing MuJoCo; link the copy bundled with unitree_rl_mjlab.
  • Edit simulate/config.yaml as in the table.
  • Build. The uint8_t error in jstest (a side tool) can be ignored.
ln -s "/home/daikai/Robot Unitree/unitree_rl_mjlab/simulate/mujoco" \
      "/home/daikai/Robot Unitree/unitree_mujoco/simulate/mujoco"

cd "/home/daikai/Robot Unitree/unitree_mujoco/simulate"
rm -rf build && mkdir build && cd build
cmake .. && make -j8

config.yaml

KeyValue
robot"g1"
robot_scene"scene_29dof.xml"
domain_id0
interface"lo"
use_joystick1
joystick_type"xbox"
joystick_deviceFIFO simulate/vjs0 (step 5), or /dev/input/js0 with a real gamepad
Exit checkBuilt target unitree_mujoco appears; on launch it lists 29 joints and "Using unitree_hg DDS IDL for robot g1".

5

Keyboard as a virtual gamepad

Python 3 · no sudo

Stand in for an Xbox gamepad: a script writes joystick events into a FIFO that the simulator reads like /dev/input/js0.

Key map

KeyGamepadEffect
1LT + ↑FixStand (stand up)
2RT + AVelocity (walk)
3RB + AMimic dance1
0LT + BPassive (emergency stop)
w s a dleft stickforward, back, sideways
q e / xright stick / releaseturn / stop moving

Good to know

  • Script: unitree_mujoco/simulate/keyboard_joystick.py.
  • Run it in a real terminal window (Ctrl+Alt+T) because it reads key presses. Run from the chat box, it gets closed.
  • Start it before or together with the simulator; it waits until the simulator opens the FIFO.
python3 "/home/daikai/Robot Unitree/unitree_mujoco/simulate/keyboard_joystick.py"
Exit checkThe script prints "Đã kết nối." (connected) and the key map.

Output

FIFO simulate/vjs0
6

Run sim2sim

3 terminal windows · Ctrl+Alt+T

Let model 30000 drive the virtual robot and watch the dance.

Open in this order

# Window 1: virtual gamepad
python3 "/home/daikai/Robot Unitree/unitree_mujoco/simulate/keyboard_joystick.py"

# Window 2: simulator
cd "/home/daikai/Robot Unitree/unitree_mujoco/simulate/build" && ./unitree_mujoco

# Window 3: controller
cd "/home/daikai/Robot Unitree/unitree_rl_mjlab/deploy/robots/g1/build" && ./g1_ctrl --network=lo

Keys (in window 1)

  1. 1: stand up, wait about 2 seconds.
  2. 2: walk mode; try w/s, then x.
  3. 3: start dance1.
  4. 0: emergency stop if it falls.

If the robot falls right at launch: press Backspace in the MuJoCo window to reset, then press 1.

Exit checkThe robot finishes the dance without falling, joints don't shake or jerk, and the g1_ctrl log shows Loaded motion file 'dance1_subject2'.

If it falls or shakes: compare with play.py in mjlab; if mjlab is fine but this isn't, check params/deploy.yaml (kp/kd, joint order) and go back to step 1.

Move to the real G1

Real robot · Ethernet cable · 2 people

Run the same g1_ctrl, changing only the network interface, once step 6 passes.

Suspend the robotPower on while it hangs, wait for zero-torque mode.
Debug modePress L2 + R2 on the Unitree remote to enter debug mode.
NetworkSet the PC to 192.168.123.222/24; find the interface name with ifconfig.
ControlUse the Unitree remote that ships with the robot, not the keyboard.
cd "/home/daikai/Robot Unitree/unitree_rl_mjlab/deploy/robots/g1/build"
./g1_ctrl --network=enp5s0   # replace with your interface name

Errors hit and how they were fixed

ErrorCauseFix
Could NOT find Boostapt packages not installedStep 2, apt install
cd: ~/unitree_sdk2: No such fileSkipped git cloneClone first, then build
unitree_mujoco cmake can't find MuJoCoMissing simulate/mujoco folderCreate the symlink (step 4)
uint8_t error in jstest.ccSide tool missing <cstdint>Ignore; the simulator still builds
Error: Joystick open failed.No gamepad connectedUse the virtual gamepad (step 5)
libddsc.so.0: cannot open shared objectLibrary cache not refreshedsudo ldconfig

Buying a gamepad for simulation

Xbox Wireless ControllerGenuine Microsoft; plug in USB-C and it works on Linux.
Logitech F310 / F710Cheap and durable; set the back switch to X mode.
8BitDo Ultimate C / 2CGood value; select X-input mode.

Pick an XInput controller. Avoid PS4/PS5 or no-name pads, whose button layout differs. With a real gamepad, set joystick_device back to /dev/input/js0.

Compiled from a working session on 5 Nov 2026 on the user's machine (Ubuntu, GCC 13.3, MuJoCo 3.3.6). Steps 1–5 were built and checked; the virtual gamepad FIFO was tested to send correctly formatted events. A full run of step 6 and all of step 7 are not yet verified.
